question: Whether a driverless source records a mailslot a server made and a client opened by its name - the mailslot's creation, the client's open, each message written and read with the size asked for and the size moved, each close - under the two candidates the inspection found: the kernel's classic file I/O class, collected by a private system logger, and Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-File at the keywords ADR-003 measured named pipes under.
answer: In 3 runs, machine-wide and nothing lost - 32 messages of up to 2,048 bytes, 64 messages of up to 400 bytes, 5 ms apart, 8 messages of up to 32,768 bytes - neither source recorded the mailslot's creation, the client's open, any of the 104 messages written or read, or a close: no record named the mailslot, and none of the two processes' reads or writes had a message's size or a read's. Each source recorded about 1,500 records of each process's own files in the same session - the truth logs' writes among them - so it was live for them. No driverless source records a mailslot on this build: the tier is Unsupported (ADR-085).
method: Each run: the lab probe started a private system logger of its own with the kernel's process, thread, file I/O and file I/O init flags, and an owned session enabling Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-File at keywords 0x3F0, both machine-wide, then ran the workload. A record is the mailslot's where it names the run's own name or carries a file object such a record named; the two processes' reads and writes of the truth's sizes are counted apart, as a mailslot's would carry no name where its creation was not recorded. The probe writes counts alone, never a file's name or an address.
